name: Anticipation → strike → follow-through → settle
definition: A small move opposite to the main action, then a fast action, overshoot and settle.
how: Wind-up opposite direction 4–8 F; action 2–6 F (can be as short as 3–4 F if the anticipation was readable); overshoot 2–4 F; settle 6–10 F.
purpose: Make fast actions readable and give them force.
use_when: any punch, throw, jump, dash, hand thrusting a product to camera
avoid_when: slow, gentle actions (anticipation minimal — meaning is in the action itself)

examples.work: The Adventures of André and Wally B. (1984)
examples.note: zip-off is 3–4 frames but anticipated long enough to read

ai_image_prompt: character in a deep wind-up pose before throwing, body coiled away from the throw direction, strong line of action, clear silhouette
ai_video_prompt: the character winds up, pulling back, then throws quickly forward, arm follows through and the body settles
common_mistakes: anticipation in the same direction as the action
action so fast with no anticipation that it is missed
check: Pause on the anticipation frame: can a viewer guess what comes next? Is the action ≥2 F and the settle ≥6 F?

name: Take (shock reaction)
definition: Cartoon reaction to a surprise: tiny squash, stretch up with wide eyes, hold, then settle.
how: Eyes/brows switch first (0 F), squash 3 F, shoot up with stretch 4 F, land small squash 5 F, settle 6 F, then hold 12+ F so the joke/shock reads.
purpose: Sell surprise or a reveal; comedy beat.
use_when: reveals, jump scares, punchlines, 'the price is…' promo beat
avoid_when: every line of a dialogue (loses power)
ai_image_prompt: cartoon character mid-take: eyes huge, body stretched upward, hair standing up, hands open, plain background
ai_video_prompt: the character jumps back in surprise, eyes widening, then freezes in a shocked pose
common_mistakes: take too long (> 1 s) before the hold
check: Eyes change on the first frame; the hold after the take is ≥ 12 F.
rig_js: R.emote(P, t, 'shock')  // eyes wide + brows up + mouth O + jolt(30) + pose open + tuft overshoot

name: Jolt / startle (small take)
definition: A smaller startle without the cartoon hold; used inside dialogue.
how: Squash 3 F → up 4 F (h ≈ 18–30 px at s=1) → land 5 F → settle 6 F = 18 F.
purpose: Quick physical reaction to a sound or line.
use_when: door bell, phone ring, sudden line
ai_video_prompt: the man flinches slightly at a sudden sound and looks up
check: Is there a visible or audible cause on the same frame (±1 F)?

name: Head turn (timing = meaning)
definition: Turning the head between two poses; the number of inbetweens changes the meaning (Thomas & Johnston table).
how: Eyes move first (3 F), head starts 2 F later, body 6 F later. Pick duration by meaning: 2 F = hit by force; 4 F = hit/flinch; 6 F = nervous twitch; 8 F = dodging; 10 F = crisp order; 12 F = friendly 'over here'; 14 F = sees something desirable; 16 F = tries to look closer; 18 F = searching; 20 F = appraising; 22 F = stretching (24 fps, drawings on 2s — our approximation).
purpose: Control emotional meaning of a look with one number.
avoid_when: turning on 2s while the camera pans (judder)

examples.note: 0–10 inbetweens each given a meaning; quoted in Lasseter 1987

ai_video_prompt: the woman slowly turns her head to look at the shelf, thoughtful, eyes leading the head
check: Compare the chosen duration with the meaning table; eyes must start before the head.
rig_js: R.look(P, t, dx, dy)  // default: pupils 3F, face/head +2F over 8–9F, hair +3F, body +6F over 12F; big turns blink

timing_table_inbetweens.7: tries to get a better look

name: Eyes lead, head follows, body last
definition: Successive breaking of joints for a look: eyes → head → torso.
how: Pupils 3 F; head +2 F over 9 F; torso +6 F over 12 F; hair lags +3 F.
purpose: Makes looks feel alive and motivated.
avoid_when: robots/mechanical characters (move all at once on purpose)
ai_video_prompt: her eyes flick to the door first, then her head turns, then her shoulders follow
common_mistakes: all parts start on the same frame
check: Frame-step: eyes move before anything else.
rig_js: R.look(P, t, dx, dy, { body: true })
gsap_hint: stagger: eyes t, head t+2/24, torso t+6/24

name: Blink
definition: Lids close and open; a natural blink is very short.
how: Close 2 F, closed 1 F, open 3 F (≈ 0.25 s). Natural rate: every 2–5 s, ~15% doubles; blink to hide eye travel on big turns; no blinks during shocked stares.
purpose: Keeps a held character alive; punctuates thoughts.
ai_video_prompt: the character blinks naturally while listening
check: Count blinks in a 10 s hold: about 2–4, irregular.

name: Moving hold (breathing idle)
definition: A held pose that keeps tiny motion: breathing, blinks, hair drift, camera drift.
how: Chest scaleY +1–2% over ~3.2 s cycle, shoulders 2 F later; blinks every 2–5 s; camera drift 3–6 px. In anime/limited style: only mouth + blinks.
purpose: Prevent the 'dead freeze' of rigs/CG during dialogue and VO.
use_when: any shot where a character holds > 1 s
avoid_when: a deliberate freeze-frame for comedy/drama (make it obviously a freeze)
ai_video_prompt: the boy stands still listening, breathing softly, blinking now and then
check: Pause on a hold for 3 s: something must move subtly.
rig_js: R.breathe(P, t0, t1, .014, 3.2); R.blinks(P, t0, t1); R.listen(P, t0, t1); cam.drift(t0, t1, 4)

name: Overshoot & settle
definition: After arriving, a part goes slightly past the target and returns — follow-through on stop.
how: Overshoot 2–4 F (3–8% of the move), settle 6–10 F. GSAP back.out(1.4–2). Never on opacity/colour.
purpose: Give arrivals weight and life.
use_when: poses, product landing, UI cards, titles

examples.note: spatial springs damping 0.9 (slight overshoot); effects damping 1 (none)

ai_video_prompt: the eyeglasses slide into place and settle with a tiny bounce
common_mistakes: elastic wobble 3+ times on a premium product
check: Overshoot visible on at most 1–2 frames, then still.

name: Bounce (ball / product drop)
definition: Object falls (accelerating), contacts with squash, rises (decelerating) lower each time.
how: Fall power2.in; contact frame squash (volume kept: sx=1/√sy); rise power2.out; each bounce ~60% height and shorter in time. Rubber: big squash; product/glass: ≤3% squash or none.
purpose: Show material and weight through timing/spacing.
use_when: logo drops, toy-like products, cartoon objects
avoid_when: premium rigid products with big squash

examples.note: small squash judged as plausible as physics; larger tolerated if material unknown

ai_video_prompt: the eyeglasses case drops onto the table, bounces once slightly and settles
check: Frame spacing widens while falling and narrows while rising; squash only on the contact frame(s).

name: Walk (front-facing storybook)
definition: Alternate leg lifts with body bob (down on contact, up on passing) and counter-swinging arms.
how: Step 12 F normal (0.5 s), 10 F brisk, 15–16 F elderly/tired; bob down 20% of step, up 30%; head counter-rotates; hair lags 3 F; 4 F lean-in anticipation and a settle at the end.
purpose: Move a frontal puppet across frame.
ai_video_prompt: the boy walks toward camera at a relaxed pace
common_mistakes: arms swing with the same-side leg
check: Footstep SFX lands on each step start (contact).
gsap_hint: per step: leg y -14 over st/2 sine.out, back sine.in; bob +3.5 then -7

name: Walk (profile, contact/down/passing/up)
definition: Four key poses per step; stance foot planted while the body passes over it (no foot slide).
how: Step 12 F; contact → down (lowest, 20% of step) → passing (foot lifted) → up (highest) → next contact; stride = 2·leg·sin(A), stance leg rotation linear so the foot doesn't slide.
purpose: Believable travel in profile.
ai_video_prompt: side view, the woman walks from left to right across the shop
common_mistakes: foot slide (stride not matched to travel speed)
check: Freeze on each contact frame: front heel down, legs spread; planted foot x-position constant over the step.
gsap_hint: stance leg rotation ease:'none' to avoid slide

name: Run cycle
definition: Like a walk but with a flight phase (no foot on the ground).
how: 4–8 F per step (fast run 4–6 F, jog 8 F) at 24 fps; strong forward lean; bigger arm pump; contact squash; usually on 1s for speed.
purpose: Urgency, chase, comedy dash.

examples.note: 4–8 F per step listed as industry practice in curriculum 06 notes

ai_video_prompt: the boy runs across the street, leaning forward, arms pumping
common_mistakes: walk cycle sped up (no flight phase)
check: There must be frames with both feet off the ground.
rig_js: (not in rig.js yet — build from walkSide with step .25 and a flight pose)

name: Hand wave
definition: Raise arm to a wave pose, forearm oscillates at the elbow, lags behind the upper arm.
how: Raise 8 F; each swing 5 F (sine.inOut); 2–3 cycles; forearm starts 2 F after upper arm (overlap); end with settle.
purpose: Greeting, goodbye, attention.

examples.note: chapter title 'Timing, staggers, wave and whip'

ai_video_prompt: she waves hello warmly, wrist loose
common_mistakes: stiff whole-arm wave from the shoulder
check: The hand trails the forearm by 1–2 F on direction changes.

name: Nod (yes)
definition: Head dips and returns; small and quick for agreement, slow for understanding.
how: Each nod 9 F (down 4 F, up 5 F); 1–3 nods; listener nods every 1.6–3 s.
purpose: Agreement, listening.
avoid_when: while the same character speaks every word
ai_video_prompt: the old woman nods gently while listening
check: Nod ≤ 6 px at s=1 for normal agreement.

name: Head shake (no)
definition: Head rotates side to side and returns to centre.
how: Each swing 6 F, ±7°, 3 swings + 6 F return; slower (8–10 F) for sadness/disbelief.
purpose: Refusal, disbelief.
ai_video_prompt: he shakes his head slowly in disbelief
check: Last swing smaller than the first (decay).

name: Smear frame
definition: 1–2 frames of stretched/blurred drawing on a very fast move.
how: Max 2 F; stretch along the motion (scale 1.35 + directional blur); place between two distant keys.
purpose: Keep very fast motion readable.

examples.note: cartoon motion blur keeps fast objects comprehensible

ai_image_prompt: smear frame of a cartoon character dashing right, elongated body, speed lines
check: Step through: smear appears on 1–2 frames only, aligned with the motion.

name: View swap turn (front ↔ profile)
definition: Turn a 2D puppet by swapping drawings on a small squash and a blink.
how: Squash 3 F before; swap on 1 F; settle 5 F with back.out; blink 1 F before the swap.
purpose: Fake rotation in 2D without a 3D model.
use_when: any change of facing in rig clips
check: No visible pop at normal speed.

name: Animate on twos (limited look)
definition: Character poses update every 2nd frame (12 drawings/s at 24 fps); camera stays on 1s.
how: Snap tween start/end to the 2-frame grid and step the ease; keep lip-sync and camera on 1s; switch to 1s for a key action ('sakuga').
purpose: Hand-drawn/anime feel, deliberate stylisation.

examples.note: stepped timing function = on-n-s in CSS

check: Count unique poses per second: 12 for the character, 24 for camera.
gsap_hint: ease: 'steps(12)' per 1 s tween, or CSS animation-timing-function: steps(n, jump-end)

name: Lip-sync
definition: Mouth shapes follow the audio; consonant closures shown; mouth slightly leads sound.
how: Mouth leads audio by 1 F; vowels hold ≥ 2 F; closures (ม บ ป พ) 2 F before vowel; return to rest; head accents on loud peaks only.
purpose: Believable speech.

examples.note: ~200 ms asymmetric window; visual lead tolerated more

check: Scrub at 24 fps: closed mouth on every /m/ /b/ /p/.
rig_js: R.talk(P, t0, ENV[n], TEXT[n])  // envelope from _craft/visemes.py

name: Kinetic text: staggered entrance
definition: Letters/words/lines enter one after another with deceleration.
how: Per word 2–4 F offset, each word 6–9 F with power2.out or M3 emphasized decelerate (0.05,0.7,0.1,1); total stagger ≤ ~0.6 s; then hold readable ≥ 1.5 s.
purpose: Show reading order and hierarchy; avoid grouping everything as one.
use_when: titles, captions, beat-clip words, promo lines

examples.note: animation TYPE matters most; speed/dynamics amplify

common_mistakes: text still moving when it must be read
check: Read-at-rest ≥ 1.5 s; entrance uses decelerate.

name: Product hero reveal
definition: Hero object enters fast and glides to rest, then supporting info staggers in.
how: Product 15 F M3 emphasized decelerate; callouts stagger 4 F; price back.out(1.4) 9 F then hold ≥ 1.5 s; exit emphasized accelerate (0.3,0,0.8,0.15) 9 F.
purpose: Premium, confident arrival; clear hierarchy.
ai_image_prompt: eyeglasses hero shot on clean background, empty negative space for title, no text
ai_video_prompt: eyeglasses rotate slowly on a turntable, studio light, static camera
common_mistakes: price moving while it should be read
check: Eye goes to product first, price readable at rest.

name: Impact camera shake
definition: Short decaying camera shake on an impact.
how: 0.3–0.6 s, 8–20 px, ~18 Hz, decays to 0; starts on the impact frame with the SFX.
purpose: Sell force of impact without animating more.
ai_video_prompt: camera shakes briefly as the door slams
check: Shake and hit SFX start on the same frame.
gsap_hint: random offsets decaying per 1/18 s step
